deities: Lord Shiva (Shiva Lingam in the inner sanctum, principal deity)
Gangadhareshwara (58-foot concrete sculpture of Shiva holding Goddess Ganga in his matted locks)
Ganesha, Parvati, Ayyappa, Vishnu, Kartikeya and Hanuman (sculptures on the 3-tier Rajagopuram and shrines)

history.dynasty: Pandya (origins traditionally linked to the Pandya dynasty; modern revival managed by the Aazhimala Shiva Temple Devaswom Trust)
history.period: Believed to date to the 8th century AD per popular accounts; one travel source dates the present temple to the 16th century - conflicting claims, exact antiquity unverified
history.summary: The Aazhimala Siva Temple is a cliffside shrine on the Arabian Sea coast near Vizhinjam in Thiruvananthapuram district. Its name combines the Malayalam words 'Aazhi' (sea) and 'Mala' (hill); its original name is Aazhimala Pulinkudi Sree Mahadeva Temple (Pullinkudi from the cheetahs once found in the area). Local folklore links the rock caves to the Mahabharata: the Pandavas are said to have hidden here during their exile, and Bhima is said to have struck a rock with his knee (one account says elbow) to create a freshwater stream for Draupadi/Panchali that still exists. The temple blends Dravidian and traditional Kerala styles and has a colourful 3-tier Rajagopuram. It shot to global fame after the unveiling of the 58-foot (18-metre) Gangadhareshwara sculpture of Shiva by local artist P.S. Devadathan - reported as Kerala's tallest Shiva sculpture, six years in the making; construction began on 2 April 2014 and it was unveiled to the public in late 2021 (one source dates the public opening to 31 December 2020 - verify). A meditation hall and an ancient cave, said to have been used by sages, lie below the statue. NOTE: the CSV town 'Thiruvananthapuram' is the district; the temple is at Aazhimala near Vizhinjam, south of Thiruvananthapuram city - the town field here records Vizhinjam.

name: Aazhimala Siva Temple
town_description: Vizhinjam is a coastal town in Thiruvananthapuram district, Kerala, south of Thiruvananthapuram city, known for its historic port (now an international transshipment port), the Kovalam beach belt nearby, and the cliffside Aazhimala shrine at Pullinkudi/Mulloor.

travel.airport: Thiruvananthapuram International Airport is the nearest airport - verify road distance locally.
travel.railway: Thiruvananthapuram Central is the nearest major railway station - verify road distance locally.
travel.road: On Azhimala Temple Road near Vizhinjam, off the Vizhinjam-Kovalam coastal route; a viewpoint overlooking Chowar Beach sits adjacent to the temple.

visitor_information.best_time: Early morning or around 4:30 PM to avoid crowds; October to February for pleasant coastal weather.
visitor_information.opening_hours: 5:00 AM to 11:00 AM and 5:00 PM to 8:00 PM daily (velpu.com) - verify before visiting.
